title: 🚀 NASA Tests the New RS-25 Engine... 200 Seconds of Fire for the Return to the Moon!
body: 🚀 NASA Tests the New RS-25 Engine... 200 Seconds of Fire for the Return to the Moon!

On November 18, NASA tested the developmental RS-25 engine number 10001 on the Fred Haise Test Stand at the Stennis Space Center in Mississippi, and the burn lasted the full planned 3 minutes and 20 seconds, that is, 200 seconds of fire and smoke.

The engine tested is developmental and will never fly; its purpose is to collect data to improve the performance and reliability of RS-25 engines in upcoming Artemis missions to the Moon, in cooperation with the prime contractor L3Harris Technologies.
The four RS-25 engines together generate up to two million pounds of thrust for the giant SLS rocket, and NASA plans the Artemis 4 mission, which includes landing on the Moon's surface, in 2028.
Simply put: an engine that will never fly, but testing it decides the safety of those who will fly; so will humanity return to the Moon this time to stay?
